transcript:
14:30 Jared Kim (AE): Hey everybody, good afternoon, this is Jared from Redwood Inference. Thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call?
14:31 Leah Carter (CISO): Leah here.
14:31 Omar Ruiz (Cloud Ops): Omar here.
14:31 Nadia Petrov (Compliance): Nadia on the line.
14:31 Tim Wu (Platform): Tim here.
14:32 Jared Kim: Great. I'll hand off to Priya and Marcus to go through the controls mapping doc and then we can circle back on any gaps.
14:33 Priya Anand (SE): Hi team. Quick agenda, we'll cover what artifacts are in our trust center, the SOC 2 Type II scope, ISO 27001 certification, how our controls map to typical bank controls, and then dive into encryption and key management.
14:34 Omar: Sounds good. Important for us — data residency, we need to know where logs live and whether log export can stay in our VPC.
14:35 Priya: Yep. So high level, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II covering security and availability in scope; ISO 27001 certificate is for our control framework. We host artifacts in a trust center link we can share, and evidence packages can be made available under NDA.
14:36 Nadia: When you say evidence packages, do you mean the full working papers or just the summary mapping? For audits we need runnable evidence for specific controls, not just summary docs.
14:36 Marcus Li: Good question. We typically provide the attestation (SOC 2 report) and the certificate plus a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps SOC/ISO clauses to Redwood controls and evidence types. Full working papers are usually restricted but we can facilitate a reviewer access process or provide extracts under a scoped NDA.
14:37 Leah: Also, SSO and provisioning—how mature is your SCIM/SAML implementation? We need automated user lifecycle with role mapping to enforce separation of duties.
14:38 Priya: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM provisioning. Role-based access control is implemented; common roles are admin, devops, read-only, and auditor. There is an RBAC matrix in the console. One caveat: some parts of the infra for Dedicated deployments use customer-provided IAM controls + our app-level RBAC.
14:39 Tim: Can you confirm whether we can use customer-managed keys? We need CMEK for highly regulated workloads so that we control rotation and revocation.
14:40 Marcus: Short answer: yes for Private and certain Dedicated options. We support integration with KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). For hosted plans we have our managed KMS, but we can enable 'bring-your-own-key'/CMEK in Private deployments or Dedicated with customer KMS connectivity.
14:41 Omar: Any limitations on KV cache encryption or in-memory ephemeral keys?
14:42 Priya: The K V cache — sorry, KV cache — is encrypted in transit and at rest. For Dedicated and Private, keys can be customer-managed at rest. In-memory is ephemeral and not persisted beyond the session; we have boundary controls to limit cache lifetime.
14:43 Leah: Audit logs — where are they stored and for how long? We need 2 years retention for certain logs, with ability to ship to our SIEM.
14:44 Marcus: Default retention in our hosted product is 90 days, with options to export logs to S3/Blob or stream via syslog/Kafka for longer retention. Dedicated deployments can be configured to retain longer and to store logs either in customer VPC or in a dedicated logging bucket.
14:45 Nadia: Is the audit trail tamper-evident? Are logs signed or timestamped in a way that meets our auditors' checks?
14:46 Priya: We maintain append-only storage with immutability options for Dedicated/Private. For hosted, we can provide digital signatures and time-based hash chains for logs upon request for audit purposes. We'll note that as part of the evidence package.
14:47 Tim: On SAML user mapping, can we sync groups into RBAC roles so we don't have to manage users manually?
14:48 Marcus: Yes, SCIM group sync to role mapping is supported. There may be a small setup step in the console; we'll provide a runbook.
14:49 Omar: Does Redwood have ISO control mappings for the common bank controls like A.10 cryptographic controls, A.9 access control and A.12 operations?
14:50 Priya: Yes, the controls mapping spreadsheet includes ISO 27001 clause mappings (A.5–A.18) to our implemented controls, the responsible owner, and sample evidence.
14:51 Leah: About the SOC 2 Type II report — can we get the full report or just a redacted copy? Our procurement wants the full report for risk review.
14:52 Jared: We can provide the full SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. There's a standard access process — upload to trust center and then we send a one-time access link to your security mailbox.
14:53 Nadia: Will the trust center show which tests were performed and test period dates? Auditors look for the testing period and scope.
14:54 Marcus: Yes — the SOC 2 report includes the period covered and the list of control tests performed. We'll also include the control exceptions if any and remediation notes.
14:55 Tim: Procurement will ask for specific contractual language around CMEK and key escrow. Do you have standard clause text we can review?
14:55 Jared: We do — I can share sample contract language for customer-managed keys and a model SLA for Dedicated/Private deployments.
14:56 Omar: What about pen tests and vulnerability scanning evidence — internal and third-party?
14:57 Priya: We conduct quarterly internal scans and annual third-party penetration tests. Summary reports and remediation tracking are part of the evidence set; full detailed pentest reports are typically provided under an NDA.
14:58 Leah: Regarding data residency: we need to ensure that training data and derivatives are not exported outside our region EMEA for certain workloads. Do you support region pinning?
14:59 Marcus: Yes, region/partition pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private. For hosted, we have region routing and can pin to EU regions; we can also set routing policies at the tenant level. We'll note any model replication considerations.
15:00 Nadia: For auditors, will you map your control owners to Heritage Bank's control IDs? That mapping saves a ton of time.
15:01 Priya: That's exactly what the controls mapping spreadsheet does — we'll map Heritage control IDs to Redwood controls and provide expected evidence artifacts and owner contact. We'll create one tailored mapping for your in-scope systems.
15:02 Tim: Can you provide an example mapping row?
15:03 Priya: Sure — example: Heritage control "CR-01 - Data Encryption at Rest" maps to Redwood control "Encryption:DataAtRest-01", evidence: KMS config snapshot, key rotation policy, key ARN, and SOC 2 control test id.
15:04 Omar: A note on log export: we'd like logs to live in our S3 in eu-west-1 and be write-once. Are there objections?
15:05 Marcus: No objection — we can stream logs to your S3 with write-once lifecycle policies for immutability; for Dedicated/Private we can also store them behind your VPC endpoint.
15:06 Leah: Will you allow our auditors to do remote control tests or read-only queries during their review?
15:07 Jared: We have a read-only reviewer role and we can provision time-bounded access; for live tests we coordinate with our security team.
15:08 Nadia: One practical ask — can you include a column in the mapping spreadsheet for 'evidence delivery method' (trust center / NDA / reviewer access)?
15:09 Priya: Absolutely. We'll add that column and pre-fill with typical delivery methods.
15:10 Jared: Quick recap and next steps: we'll upload SOC 2 Type II and ISO artifacts to the trust center by EOD tomorrow, Priya will deliver a controls mapping draft by 2025-06-09, Tim will send log retention specifics, and we'll schedule a technical deep dive next week to walk auditors through evidence.
15:11 Leah: That covers it from my side. Thanks — this helps align expectations.
15:12 Omar: Thanks all.
15:13 Tim: Thanks.
15:14 Nadia: Thank you.
15:15 Jared: Appreciate it — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the trust center link.
15:16 [call ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings of 'KV cache' as 'K V cache' and 'Redwood' as 'Red wood' in auto transcript. Some overlaps in speakers at 14:55-14:58 were merged.
